espn-603993.headline: Argentina bring everyone; Ireland count who is missing
beats: Felipe Contepomi has named his strongest squad of the year for this tour. Captain Julián Montoya is back, along with over a dozen others who missed the home games against Australia. Without them, Argentina still drew the last of those 28–28.

Ireland are going the other way. Caelan Doris and Jack Conan are both out of the back row. Sam Prendergast is a doubt at out-half with a wrist injury picked up in training. Uncapped Ulster pair James McNabney and Jamie Benson are in the squad.
Ireland's last game was in July, a 40–21 loss to New Zealand. Lose this one and they drop to fourth in the world, below France, after holding third since that month.
Both sides then play opponents still without a point, so this is the game that will tell them anything.

espn-603994.headline: A draw in Turin would cost South Africa top spot
beats: South Africa are first in the world and first in the Nations Championship, level on points with New Zealand. Anything short of a win at Allianz Stadium hands the world No.1 ranking to New Zealand.
Italy have not won since beating England in March, and conceded 47 and 57 in their last two games. When these sides last met, in November 2025, Italy were at home and lost 14–32.
South Africa's last outing was a 38–42 loss to Australia in September: six tries scored, still beaten. They have since lost a key player for this game and the trips to France and Ireland.
Six days after Turin they are at the Stade de France, where François Cros has been waiting since a one-point World Cup quarter-final in 2023.

espn-603995.headline: Scotland score plenty. So, lately, do New Zealand
beats: Scotland have put 47 on Argentina and 50 on France this year, and let in 38 and 40 doing it. New Zealand put 50 and 43 on Australia in October, straight after three defeats in a row by South Africa.
Graham Henry says that series has forced New Zealand to rethink how they train. They reach Europe with a triple injury blow to absorb as well.

Scotland lost 17–25 at Murrayfield on 8 November 2025, a margin of eight against a side that has since conceded 43 to South Africa. Win this time and Scotland go above England into fifth in the world.
The sides meet again in Dunedin before next year's World Cup, Scotland's first away game against New Zealand in 27 years. Whatever is settled in Edinburgh gets a second hearing.

espn-603996.headline: Wales won by a point last year. Japan now sit above them
beats: Wales won 24–23 when the sides last met in Cardiff, on 15 November 2025. Since then Japan have won the Pacific Nations Cup, beating Fiji 20–15 in the September final, and climbed from 12th to 9th. Wales have slipped from 10th to 11th.

Neither side arrives in good shape. Wales have not played since July, when they lost 43–0 away to South Africa without scoring a try. Japan lost 34–28 at home to Fiji in October, the side they beat in that final, and it spoiled their union's centenary.
Any Wales win puts them back above Japan in the rankings and leaves Japan 12th at best. In the Nations Championship a single point separates them, in 9th and 10th.
A week later Wales host New Zealand and Japan visit England. This is the one both can win.

espn-603997.headline: Jake White's Fiji get France before South Africa do
beats: White's first game in charge was a 34–28 win in Tokyo over Eddie Jones' Japan, a month after Japan had beaten Fiji 20–15 in the Pacific Nations Cup final. He came away saying Fiji can be a force at next year's World Cup.

The Nations Championship has been less kind. Fiji have no points from three games and conceded 73 to England at home in July. France scored six tries in each of their last two, 42–26 in Australia and 42–15 in Japan, and beat Fiji 34–21 at home last November.
A Fiji win would drop France to fifth, below England, five days before South Africa visit the Stade de France.
François Cros says France lost the 2023 quarter-final to South Africa in the build-up: "we didn't lose on the field, we lost it before." This is the build-up.

espn-603998.headline: One Australia win and England are seventh
beats: England have been fifth in every world ranking since July. Any Australia win at Allianz Stadium, by any margin, puts the visitors fifth and drops England to seventh, below Scotland as well.
Australia are not obviously the side to do it. They beat South Africa 42–38 in September, then conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in a fortnight.

England have not played since beating Argentina 31–24 in July. They won the last meeting 25–7 at home, on 1 November 2025. Maro Itoje is back in the 36-man squad, and Joe Marchant is recalled for the first time since the 2023 World Cup as injuries thin the midfield.
England host Japan next. Australia go to Scotland, the other side a win here would put them above.
